en: Test for English Majors 2014.
zh: 2014年英语专业全国统一考试。

en: Grade 8.
zh: 专业八级。

en: Part 1 Listening Comprehension.
zh: 第一部分：听力理解。

en: Section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节：短讲。

en: In this section you will hear a mini-lecture.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段短讲。

en: You will hear the mini-lecture once only.
zh: 这段短讲只播放一遍。

en: While listening to the mini-lecture, please complete the gap-filling task on Answer Sheet 1 and write no more than three words for each gap.
zh: 请边听短讲，边完成答题卡一上的填空任务；每空填写不超过三个词。

en: Make sure the word(s) you fill in is or are both grammatically and semantically acceptable.
zh: 请确保填入的词在语法和语义上都恰当。

en: You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
zh: 你可以用空白纸做笔记。

en: You have thirty seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览填空任务。

en: Now, listen to the mini-lecture.
zh: 现在请听短讲。

en: When it is over, you will be given three minutes to check your work.
zh: 短讲结束后，你将有三分钟检查作答。

en: How to Reduce Stress.
zh: 如何减轻压力。

en: Good morning. Today we look at how to reduce stress.
zh: 大家早上好。今天我们来看看如何减轻压力。

en: As you all know, life always has stressors, er, things which are causing us stress and living without stress is virtually impossible.
zh: 大家都知道，生活中总会有压力源，也就是那些让我们感到压力的事情；完全没有压力的生活几乎不可能。

en: So, if we have to live with stress, we may as well find out more about what it is, how we can deal with it and so on.
zh: 既然必须与压力共处，我们不妨多了解一下它是什么，以及如何应对它等问题。

en: What is stress then?
zh: 那么，什么是压力呢？

en: The term was originally used in physics to describe the force exerted between two touching bodies.
zh: 这个术语最初用于物理学，用来描述两个相互接触的物体之间施加的力。

en: It was strictly a term describing a physical reaction.
zh: 当时，它仅仅是一个描述物理反应的术语。

en: Then in the 1930s, a doctor named Hans Selye, S-e-l-y-e,
zh: 到了二十世纪三十年代，一位名叫汉斯·塞利的医生——姓氏拼作S-e-l-y-e——

en: first used this term to describe a human’s reaction to a demand placed on it, pleasant or not.
zh: 首次用这个术语描述人对外界要求所作出的反应，无论这种要求令人愉快与否。

en: And he included in this response things like accelerated breathing, accelerated heart rate, increased blood pressure, muscle tension and so on.
zh: 他把呼吸加快、心率加快、血压升高、肌肉紧张等都包括在这种反应之中。

en: Now, please notice that I said that stress can be pleasant or not.
zh: 请注意，我刚才说了，压力带来的感受可以愉快，也可以不愉快。

en: This response can also be pleasant or not, and stress can be both negative and positive.
zh: 这种反应也可能令人愉快或不愉快，而压力既可以是负面的，也可以是正面的。

en: Let’s take a look at positive stress.
zh: 我们先来看看正面压力。

en: Positive stress occurs in a life situation towards which one feels positively.
zh: 当人们对生活中的某种情境抱有积极感受时，就会产生正面压力。

en: Things like Christmas or getting married are usually positive events, but still stressful nonetheless.
zh: 例如圣诞节、结婚通常都是好事，但仍然会让人感到压力。

en: Another example is that pressure in a job can give some people incentive to work and excitement, but it still is stress.
zh: 再比如，工作压力可以给一些人带来工作动力和兴奋感，但它仍然是压力。

en: Negative stress is what most of us think of when we think of stress.
zh: 我们大多数人一提到压力，想到的都是负面压力。

en: And negative stress occurs logically enough in situations towards which one feels negatively.
zh: 很自然，当人们对某种情境有消极感受时，就会产生负面压力。

en: And those examples could be test-taking, a friend’s death and so on.
zh: 例如参加考试、朋友去世等。

en: But here a thing to remember is that stress in itself is not hazardous, rather the danger is in the individual’s reaction to the stress.
zh: 但要记住，压力本身并不危险，危险在于个人对压力的反应。

en: So psychologists have found that if we develop appropriate ways to cope with stressful situations,
zh: 心理学家因此发现，如果我们学会以适当的方式应对压力情境，

en: individuals can reduce the physiological harm which is caused by stress, or which can be caused by stress.
zh: 就能够减轻压力已经造成或可能造成的生理伤害。

en: And that’s what I want to talk a bit about today: what are these appropriate ways to deal with stress; how to minimize any negative reactions.
zh: 这就是我今天想谈的内容：有哪些适当的应对压力的方法，以及怎样把负面反应降到最低。

en: The first thing that most psychologists suggest is to learn to recognize your own stress signals.
zh: 大多数心理学家给出的第一条建议，是学会识别自己的压力信号。

en: We all have different types of stress signals, but individuals should monitor themselves for stress signals
zh: 每个人的压力信号各不相同，但我们都应该留意自身的这些信号，

en: so that they can focus on minimizing or acknowledging the stress before it gets out of control.
zh: 以便在压力失控之前，着手减轻它，或者正视它的存在。

en: And common early signs for many people include irritability, insomnia, weight loss or even weight gain, smoking, drinking, increases in small errors.
zh: 许多人常见的早期信号包括烦躁、失眠、体重减轻或增加、吸烟、饮酒，以及小差错增多。

en: All kinds of things that people get which could be an early signal of stress.
zh: 人们身上出现的各种情况，都可能是压力的早期信号。

en: You can consider ways to protect yourself when you start seeing these signs coming on,
zh: 开始察觉这些迹象时，就可以考虑如何保护自己。

en: so you might decide to withdraw from a stressful situation or reward yourself with equal amounts of low stress activity time.
zh: 比如，选择暂时离开压力情境，或者奖励自己等量时间，去参加压力较小的活动。

en: That’s really the first important way to deal with stress appropriately.
zh: 这就是恰当应对压力的第一种重要方法。

en: A second important way to deal with stress is to pay attention to your body’s demands.
zh: 第二种重要方法，是关注身体的需要。

en: Most psychologists are finding that a good exercise program, good nutrition, decreases the amount of stress, or the effect of stress on the body or in the mind.
zh: 大多数心理学家发现，良好的锻炼安排和合理的营养，能够减轻压力，或者减弱压力对身体和心理的影响。

en: And this seems quite apparent because exercise can provide a stress-free environment away from your usual stressors,
zh: 这似乎很容易理解：锻炼能提供一个远离日常压力源的无压力环境，

en: and it keeps your body busy and preoccupied with non-stressful things.
zh: 还能让身体忙起来，专注于不会造成压力的事情。

en: OK. The third thing to reduce stress is to make plans and act when appropriate.
zh: 第三种减压方法，是在适当的时候制订计划并采取行动。

en: What is suggested is that rather than wasting energy on worrying, an individual can direct his or her energy to plan the steps and act.
zh: 这条建议是说，与其把精力浪费在担忧上，不如把它用来规划步骤、采取行动。

en: And often just the planning of the action helps to reduce the stress because it reduces the worrying.
zh: 而且，往往只要开始规划行动，就有助于减轻压力，因为这样能够减少担忧。

en: And also the results of the plans or action may serve to remove or weaken the original cause of the stress.
zh: 此外，计划或行动的结果，也可能消除或削弱最初造成压力的原因。

en: Please notice that I just now said when appropriate, and this next suggestion has to do with that idea of when appropriate.
zh: 请注意，我刚才说的是“在适当的时候”，而下一条建议就与“什么时候才算适当”有关。

en: The third suggestion was to make plans and act when appropriate, rather than just sit around and worry.
zh: 第三条建议是：在适当的时候制订计划并行动，而不是干坐着担忧。

en: But the fourth plan or fourth idea says to learn to accept situations which are out of your control.
zh: 第四条建议则是：学会接受自己无法控制的情况。

en: These two then go hand in hand.
zh: 这两条建议是相辅相成的。

en: You can make plans and act when it’s appropriate, but when it’s not appropriate or when it’s impossible,
zh: 时机合适时，可以制订计划并行动；而时机不合适，或者根本无法行动时，

en: the only way is to learn to accept that some things are unchangeable, and out of your hands.
zh: 唯一的办法就是学会接受：有些事是改变不了、也不由你掌控的。

en: So, for example, if you are in traffic, lateness caused by traffic is out of your hands.
zh: 例如，如果你碰上堵车，由此造成的迟到就不是你能控制的。

en: There is no sense in getting really crazy about that.
zh: 为这件事急得发狂，并没有意义。

en: If you do so, it only increases your stress to waste energy trying to resist what’s inevitable, or what can’t be avoided.
zh: 如果这样做，把精力浪费在抗拒无法避免的事情上，只会增加自己的压力。

en: The last item that psychologists suggest is to pace your activities.
zh: 心理学家最后一条建议，是安排好活动的节奏。

en: By pace I mean giving yourself some manageable task to do at a reasonable speed.
zh: 这里的“安排节奏”，是指给自己安排能够应付的任务，以合理的速度去完成。

en: That is, you go at a speed that you can handle.
zh: 也就是说，按自己能够承受的速度去做。

en: Break your task into manageable parts, rather than try to deal with the whole task all at once.
zh: 把任务分成若干能够应付的小部分，而不是试图一次完成整个任务。

en: So as an example in your lives as students, a whole term paper might feel overwhelming.
zh: 以学生生活为例，一整篇学期论文可能让你觉得无从下手、难以招架。

en: But if you say to yourself: today I’m going to the library and gather resources; tomorrow I’m going to read three articles, and so on,
zh: 但如果你告诉自己：今天去图书馆找资料，明天读三篇文章，以此类推，

en: you will have broken this one large task, that’s writing a term paper, down into many smaller and more manageable tasks.
zh: 那么，你就把写学期论文这一项大任务，分解成了许多更小、更容易完成的任务。

en: This will certainly reduce your stress.
zh: 这肯定能够减轻你的压力。

en: OK. Having said all these, I want you to remember that the problem is not in the stressful experiences themselves.
zh: 说了这么多，我希望大家记住：问题并不在于那些带来压力的经历本身。

en: We all experience stress and stressful events.
zh: 我们都会承受压力，都会遇到令人有压力的事情。

en: The problem is in our reactions to these experiences.
zh: 问题在于我们如何对这些经历作出反应。

en: And each of us has our own limits for stress and our own ways of coping with stress.
zh: 我们每个人承受压力的限度都不同，应对压力的方式也各不相同。

en: So long as we have our own appropriate ways, stress or stressful situations can certainly be dealt with.
zh: 只要找到适合自己的方法，就一定能够应对压力或压力情境。

en: OK. That’s all for today’s lecture. See you next week.
zh: 今天的讲座就到这里，下周见。

en: Now, you have three minutes to check your work.
zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。

en: This is the end of Section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节短讲到此结束。
